icml-2024-af0821a5.appendix_review_status: A–G organization, purpose, prose claims, captions and scope reviewed; formula correctness and bibliography not reverified

A axioms; B annotations; C–E extra results; F settings; G future studies (pp.13–21)

dimensions.audience_argument: Assumes knowledge of VLMs but motivates compositionality with a horse/grass role-reversal example. Argument decomposes the diagnosis into text, image and matching, rather than presenting one undifferentiated improvement claim.
dimensions.title_abstract: Title declares task plus analytical viewpoint. Abstract follows weakness → diagnostic goal → game-theoretic metric → findings/utility; no numerical improvement is required for this diagnostic paper.
dimensions.introduction_contribution: Questions and insights are separate from the final numbered contribution list; Fig.1 makes their correspondence visible. Contributions distinguish analysis, metrics and validation.
dimensions.related_work: Three thematic paragraphs separate VLMs, compositionality and interactions; explicit contrast is black-box performance versus internal representation diagnosis.
dimensions.methods_theory: Introduces intuition and inherited Harsanyi definition before task-specific metrics. Theorem in A is attributed to prior work, not advertised as a new theoretical result.
dimensions.experiments: Each question-led section includes its own protocol and result interpretation. Tables and correlation plots support specific pattern-sensitivity claims, with dataset scope specified nearby.
dimensions.discussion_limits: Main text limits visual study to object-pair relations (p.7). G explicitly recognizes theory–practice gap and makes improvements future work, rather than claiming the proposed diagnostics already improve training.
dimensions.language: Local sentences connect question, metric, evidence and interpretation. Strong terms such as thorough/reliable occur, but empirical causal implications use partially/may; these strengths should not be copied without evidence.
dimensions.body_appendix: Main text holds definitions and representative evidence; appendix adds axioms, additional benchmarks/models, masks, experimental details and future directions, each explicitly called from the body.
dimensions.advice: For diagnostic studies, organize evidence by the diagnostic question and match each headline finding to a test. Keep intervention claims distinct from observed correlations.

claims.claim: Text encoders react to composition while image encoders and alignment are weaker
claims.scope: five evaluated VLMs, specified compositional benchmarks; extra two models in E

counterexamples: A paper can use question-led, interleaved method/results sections; a universal method-then-experiments layout would break this argument.
The abstract has no metric delta; requiring a numerical improvement in every ICML abstract would misfit a diagnostic study.
icml-2024-af0821a5.review_limitations: Writing-focused full-text audit; prose and appendix evidence organization reviewed, not a replication, proof check, figure pixel inspection or bibliographic correctness audit.

icml-2024-4207e021.paper_type: combinatorial theory and exact algorithm with numerical study
icml-2024-4207e021.appendix_review_status: A proof organization/claim links, B experiment captions and C instance table purpose reviewed; algebra not rederived
structure: Introduction and formal Definition1.1 p.1; four contributions p.2
A proofs pp.12–14, B experiments pp.14–15, C instance data p.16

dimensions.audience_argument: Defines the precise NP-hard ordering problem on page1 and then motivates ML ranking relevance. Technical readers get objective and constraints before broad empirical narrative.
dimensions.title_abstract: Short descriptive title. Abstract defines problem, computational hardness, partial-solving mechanism and two-dataset evaluation. It omits speed-up figures that appear in the introduction.
dimensions.introduction_contribution: Four explicit contributions separate conditions, fixing variables, hardness-parameter study and solver speedup; introduction states best-case 1/13 and 1/33 reductions with benchmark names.
dimensions.related_work: Compares scoring-based versus pair-cost ranking, exact solvers versus heuristics, and prior partial optimality for symmetric clustering versus asymmetric order. Novelty is a concrete structural distinction.
dimensions.methods_theory: Definition→lemma→proposition/corollary sequence includes short proofs in body and longer algebra in A. Examples show one condition does not subsume another and incompatible assignments need careful combination.
dimensions.experiments: Synthetic hardness/size sweep and LOLIB evaluation report both fixed-variable fraction and runtime, plus solver time. Hardware and code are stated. Separate-condition tests appear in body and B.
dimensions.discussion_limits: p.9 reports minimum speedups below1 (0.77/0.69) alongside maxima. Conclusion identifies marginal conditions and suggests sparsity/partial ordering extensions.
dimensions.language: Formal conditionals and existence claims maintain exact theorem boundaries. Empirical paragraphs name axes and conditions before interpreting figures; no universal performance claim.
dimensions.body_appendix: Critical definitions, conditions, short proofs, algorithms, counterexample and main experiments are in body; A holds detailed technical proofs, B per-condition curves, C benchmark mappings.
dimensions.advice: Keep assumptions adjacent to formal claims and distinguish exact guarantees from empirically variable benefits. Report overhead and unfavorable instances, not only the largest speedup.

claims.claim: Partial optimality can accelerate exact ordering solutions
claims.scope: named LOLIB IO/Spec instances; solvable-within1h Spec subset

counterexamples: Short proof steps and a formal problem definition occur in the main text; pushing all theory into an appendix would remove key evidence.
Largest solver gains coexist with slower cases, so the venue style cannot require monotonically positive improvement.
icml-2024-4207e021.review_limitations: Writing-focused full-text audit; proof statements and their explanatory organization reviewed, not algebraic proof verification or numerical reproduction.

icml-2024-09851122.appendix_review_status: A parameter-estimation proof architecture, B density-rate derivation, C identifiability, D synthetic experiments and captions reviewed; algebra not rederived
structure: Introduction integrates prior literature, problem setup, MLE, main challenges, contributions and practical implications (pp.1–3)
Standard gating: two regimes, results and proof sketch (pp.4–6)
Conclusion with limitations, future directions and technical novelty (p.9); impact p.10
A parameter proofs (pp.13–25); B density proofs (pp.25–27); C identifiability (pp.28–29); D simulations (pp.29–32)

dimensions.audience_argument: Theory readers receive a precisely defined conditional-density model and estimation objective before rates; practical MoE context motivates the model but is not the theorem domain.
dimensions.title_abstract: Title names formal model and general theory. Abstract follows unresolved classification case → two estimation regimes → collapsed-expert obstruction → modified gate; qualitative rates replace benchmark superiority.
dimensions.introduction_contribution: Long introduction contains labeled Problem Setup, MLE, Main Challenges and two contributions. Table1 aligns regimes, estimator losses and rates; Practical Implications are separately labeled.
dimensions.related_work: Prior research is integrated in the introduction by model class and identifiability/rate gap, rather than placed in an obligatory separate section.
dimensions.methods_theory: Definitions, assumptions, identifiability results and rate statements are in the body; Sec3.3 gives local/global proof strategy with three steps. Modified gates require boundedness and linear-independence conditions.
dimensions.experiments: All simulations are in D: specified synthetic binomial models, initialization near true parameters, repeated sample-size sweeps and EM iteration limits. D.1 discusses mismatch between empirical slopes and asymptotic theory; D.2.2 separately plots EM objective versus iterations.
dimensions.discussion_limits: p.9 explicitly limits theory to well-specified data; misspecification and temperature remain future work. pp.30–32 distinguish lack of global EM convergence guarantees from statistical estimator rates.
dimensions.language: Formal claims use regime conditions, almost-sure and probability qualifiers. Practical framing is broader; its language must not turn sample-size statistical rates into optimizer iteration guarantees.
dimensions.body_appendix: Body contains theorem conditions, rate table and proof sketches; A–C provide detailed proofs and borrowed-lemma attribution; D holds numerical illustration. This is a theory-first allocation, not an empirical-paper requirement.
dimensions.advice: Use an overview table when multiple conditions change the guarantee. Keep statistical rates and numerical optimization behavior distinct, and disclose initialization and empirical deviations.

claims.claim: Modified gating restores faster parameter-estimation rates in the collapsed-expert regime
claims.evidence_location: definition4.1 assumptions and A.3 pp.21–25; synthetic D.2 pp.30–32
claims.scope: specified multinomial-logistic model, bounded transformed covariates, well-specified setting; not a general LLM optimizer guarantee

counterexamples: Separate Related Work is not mandatory: the introduction integrates the literature.
A theory paper can place all synthetic experiments in an appendix while main text prioritizes conditions and proof strategy.
Numerical slopes differ from statistical rates; polishing must preserve this discrepancy.
icml-2024-09851122.review_limitations: Writing-focused full-text review of prose, theorem conditions, proof organization and appendix evidence; not rederivation of mathematical correctness, replication or bibliography verification.

icml-2024-fc8aa210.paper_type: engineering application and controlled code generation framework
icml-2024-fc8aa210.appendix_review_status: No text appendix in nine-page official final PDF; method, settings, ablations and limitations in main text. Bibliography p.9 not reverified.
structure: Algorithm: overview, data, instruction tuning, augmentation and guidance pp.3–5
Experiment settings, functional correctness, two downstream tasks, ablations pp.5–8
Discussion: current limitations and possible other domains p.8
Conclusion and impact p.8; references p.9

dimensions.audience_argument: Explains hardware-design languages, EDA flow and why downstream circuit metrics differ from generic code correctness; readers need not already be chip-design specialists.
dimensions.title_abstract: System-name plus mechanism title. Abstract describes data, tuning, discriminator and tasks; comparative GPT-4 claim has benchmark name but no numeric delta.
dimensions.introduction_contribution: Contribution bullets combine method, tuning result and augmentation. Broad first/pioneering/groundbreaking language appears; these words are source observations, not recommended venue requirements.
dimensions.related_work: Two concrete families: LLM Verilog generation and discriminator-guided controllable generation. The gap is task-specific downstream optimization rather than only syntax/function.
dimensions.methods_theory: Framework figure precedes ordered components. Code-to-Verilog/C paired training and prompt examples clarify inputs; Bayes guidance equations explain implementation but are not presented as new convergence theorems.
dimensions.experiments: Functional correctness uses both machine/human VerilogEval and pass@k; subsequent hardware tasks use selected instances and CodeLlama only. Yosys commands, hardware and training settings are in body; ablations separate functional and syntactic correctness.
dimensions.discussion_limits: Explicitly notes token-probability access prevents closed-source guidance and discriminator overhead cannot be ignored. Other-domain examples are prospective, not tested results.
dimensions.language: Source contains expansive any-task and pioneering claims. Better editorial practice retains named benchmark/model scope rather than imitating rhetoric; average node savings are not guaranteed PPA gains across all chip flows.
dimensions.body_appendix: No appendix; compact body includes experimental configuration and limits. This contradicts mandatory appendix recipes.
dimensions.advice: For cross-domain applications, explain specialist metrics and evaluators; distinguish measured synthesis-node count from inferred downstream circuit efficiency and formal safety.

claims.claim: Generated Verilog improves nodes and verification runtime
claims.scope: selected VerilogEval-human/ANSI-C designs; downstream experiments use CodeLlama; not end-to-end physical PPA or deployment validation

counterexamples: An accepted source uses promotional language; acceptance does not make that language a writing rule.
An application paper can explain specialist tooling and code examples without formal theorem sections.
No text appendix is necessary when the relevant detail fits main text.
icml-2024-fc8aa210.review_limitations: Writing-focused main-text review including experimental prose, table scope and discussion; no code replication, figure pixel audit or bibliography verification.
